# Model and source

* Citation: Jovanovic M, Topic Vucenovic V, Roganovic M, Pavlovic G, Kralj D,
  Markovic S, Svorcan P, Vucicevic K. Unlocking the Potential of Population
  Pharmacokinetic Models of Adalimumab in Patients with Crohn's Disease.
  *Pharmaceutics* 2026;18(7):788.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics18070788>
* PubMed: <https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42514869/>

The paper has two parts. It first externally evaluates eight published
adalimumab population PK models (Berends 2018, Vande Casteele 2019,
Sanchez-Hernandez 2020, Ternant 2015, Wright 2024, Spencer 2024, de Klaver
2023 and Marquez-Megias 2023; Table 1 and Table 3) against a Serbian
Crohn's disease therapeutic-drug-monitoring cohort. Those models are the
cited authors' and are not packaged here (Marquez-Megias 2023 already is, as
`MarquezMegias_2023_adalimumab`). It then develops a new model on the same
cohort, which is the model packaged here.

The new model is one-compartment with first-order subcutaneous absorption
and linear elimination, parameterised in apparent clearance (CL/F) and
apparent volume (V/F), with a combined additive and proportional residual
error. Because the dataset holds trough concentrations only, it was
estimated with NONMEM `$PRIOR NWPRI` informative priors taken from the
best-performing evaluated model, Ternant 2015: priors on V/F, the IIV of
V/F and the anti-drug-antibody (ADA) effect, with `ka` fixed at the Ternant
value of 0.15 1/day and CL/F and its IIV estimated without priors. Stepwise
covariate modelling then added C-reactive protein (CRP, log-linear) and the
dosing interval (weekly vs otherwise) on CL/F (Results 3.5):

$$
CL/F = 0.334 \cdot (1 + 6.9 \cdot ADA) \cdot (1 + 0.075 \cdot \ln CRP) \cdot (1 + 0.218 \cdot REGIMEN)
$$

# Population

The model was developed on 195 adults with Crohn's disease treated with
subcutaneous adalimumab (Humira 40 mg pre-filled pen) at the University
Medical Center 'Zvezdara', Belgrade, Serbia, who had therapeutic drug
monitoring in induction or maintenance (Table 2). Mean age was 38.05 years
(SD 11.83, range 17-67), 50.8% were female, and mean body weight was 69.44
kg (SD 13.47, range 38-105). Mean CRP was 8.46 mg/L (SD 13.47, range
0.00-72.70). 60.5% were on azathioprine and 33.8% had prior anti-TNF-alpha
therapy. The 942 trough concentrations (median time after dose 6.75 or
13.75 days, i.e. weekly or every-other-week troughs) included 15 below the
limit of quantification and 70 reported only as above 12 mg/L; the mean of
the remaining 857 was 9.58 mg/L (SD 5.69), 9.57 mg/L (SD 5.70) in
maintenance. ADA were measured on 294 occasions and were positive in 9
patients (Results 3.2).

The same metadata is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Jovanovic_2026_adalimumab")$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` | log(0.15 1/day), fixed | Table 4 'Ka (day-1)'; Results 3.5 (Ternant 2015 value) |
| `lcl` | log(0.334 L/day) | Table 4 'CL/F (L/day)', Final model; Equation (6) |
| `lvc` | log(13.5 L) | Table 4 'V/F (L)', Final model |
| `e_ada_cl` | 6.90 | Table 4 'ADA on CL/F', Final model; Equation (6) |
| `e_crp_cl` | 0.075 | Table 4 'ln(CRP) on CL/F', Final model; Equation (6) |
| `e_regi_qw_cl` | 0.218 | Table 4 'Dosing regimen on CL/F', Final model; Equation (6); Results 3.5 |
| `etalcl` | 0.333^2 = 0.1109 | Table 4 'IIVCL (%)' = 33.3, Final model |
| `etalvc` | 0.538^2 = 0.2894 | Table 4 'IIVV (%)' = 53.8, Final model |
| `addSd` | 2.71 mg/L | Table 4 'Additive residual error (mg/L)', Final model |
| `propSd` | 0.337 | Table 4 'Proportional residual error', Final model |
| CL/F covariate model | `0.334 * (1 + 6.9*ADA) * (1 + 0.075*ln(CRP)) * (1 + 0.218*REGIMEN)` | Equation (6) |
| Structure | one compartment, first-order absorption and elimination | Results 3.5; Abstract |
| Residual error | combined additive + proportional | Results 3.5; Table 4 |

# Typical-value check against the closed form

With every random effect zeroed, the steady-state trough of a
one-compartment first-order-absorption model has a closed form. The check
uses the same parameters on both sides, so the only difference is
integration error and the bound is tight.

```{r closed-form}
mod <- readModelDb("Jovanovic_2026_adalimumab")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ka <- 0.15
vc <- 13.5
cl <- 0.334 # ADA-negative, every-other-week, CRP = 1 mg/L
kel <- cl / vc
tau <- 14
dose <- 40

ss_trough <- dose * ka / (vc * (ka - kel)) *
  (exp(-kel * tau) / (1 - exp(-kel * tau)) -
    exp(-ka * tau) / (1 - exp(-ka * tau)))

# 60 doses span about 30 elimination half-lives, so the last trough is at
# steady state to well below the tolerance used here.
n_dose <- 60L
ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = dose, ii = tau, addl = n_dose - 1L, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(time = n_dose * tau, cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  mutate(ADA_POS = 0L, CRP = 1, REGI_QW = 0L)

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12)
cc_end <- sim_typ$Cc[sim_typ$time == n_dose * tau]
c(closed_form = ss_trough, simulated = cc_end)
stopifnot(abs(cc_end / ss_trough - 1) < 1e-6)
```

The typical steady-state trough on 40 mg every other week is
`r signif(ss_trough, 3)` mg/L at CRP = 1 mg/L, and the elimination
half-life is `r signif(log(2) / kel, 3)` days.

# Covariate effects on CL/F

Figure S1 of the paper plots the individual CL/F estimates against
ln(CRP). The typical-value line below is the Equation (6) relationship for
an ADA-negative patient on every-other-week dosing, over the ln(CRP) range
shown in Figure S1 (about -4.6 to 5).

```{r crp-effect}
crp_grid <- tibble(lncrp = seq(-4.6, 5, by = 0.1)) |>
  mutate(
    CRP = exp(lncrp),
    `Every other week, ADA absent` = 0.334 * (1 + 0.075 * lncrp),
    `Weekly, ADA absent` = 0.334 * (1 + 0.075 * lncrp) * 1.218
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(lncrp, CRP), names_to = "group", values_to = "cl")

ggplot(crp_grid, aes(lncrp, cl, linetype = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "ln(CRP) (CRP in mg/L)", y = "Typical CL/F (L/day)", linetype = NULL,
    title = "Typical adalimumab CL/F against ln(CRP)",
    caption = "Compare with the trend line of Figure S1 of Jovanovic 2026."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r cov-table}
tibble(
  Patient = c(
    "CRP 1 mg/L, ADA absent, every other week (reference)",
    "CRP 8.46 mg/L (cohort mean), ADA absent, every other week",
    "CRP 72.7 mg/L (cohort maximum), ADA absent, every other week",
    "CRP 1 mg/L, ADA absent, weekly",
    "CRP 1 mg/L, ADA present, every other week"
  ),
  cl = 0.334 * c(1, 1 + 0.075 * log(8.46), 1 + 0.075 * log(72.7), 1.218, 7.9)
) |>
  mutate(ratio = cl / 0.334) |>
  dplyr::rename("Typical CL/F (L/day)" = cl, "Ratio to reference" = ratio) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

# Virtual cohort

Two arms of 150 virtual patients each receive the standard induction
(160 mg at week 0, 80 mg at week 2) and then 40 mg from week 4, either every
other week or weekly. CRP is drawn from a log-normal distribution matched to
the Table 2 mean (8.46 mg/L) and SD (13.47 mg/L) and truncated to the
reported range, with the lower bound set at 0.01 mg/L because the model
is undefined at zero. ADA status is positive with probability 9/195, the
fraction of patients with any positive ADA result. Both covariates are held
constant within a patient.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260788)
set.seed(20260788)

n_per_arm <- 150L
crp_cv <- 13.47 / 8.46
crp_sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + crp_cv^2))
crp_meanlog <- log(8.46) - crp_sdlog^2 / 2

cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(2L * n_per_arm),
  treatment = rep(c("40 mg every other week", "40 mg weekly"), each = n_per_arm),
  REGI_QW = rep(c(0L, 1L), each = n_per_arm),
  CRP = pmin(pmax(rlnorm(2L * n_per_arm, crp_meanlog, crp_sdlog), 0.01), 72.7),
  ADA_POS = as.integer(runif(2L * n_per_arm) < 9 / 195)
)

cohort |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    crp_mean = mean(CRP),
    crp_median = median(CRP),
    ada_pos = sum(ADA_POS),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

```{r events}
week <- 7
end_time <- 52 * week
dose_tbl <- bind_rows(
  tibble(treatment = "40 mg every other week", time = c(0, 2 * week, seq(4 * week, end_time - 2 * week, by = 2 * week))),
  tibble(treatment = "40 mg weekly", time = c(0, 2 * week, seq(4 * week, end_time - week, by = week)))
) |>
  mutate(amt = case_when(time == 0 ~ 160, time == 2 * week ~ 80, TRUE ~ 40))

obs_times <- seq(0, end_time, by = 1)

dose_rows <- cohort |>
  inner_join(dose_tbl, by = "treatment", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
obs_rows <- cohort |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")

events <- bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("treatment", "CRP", "ADA_POS", "REGI_QW")
) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r profile, fig.height = 4.5}
sim |>
  group_by(treatment, time) |>
  summarise(
    q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05),
    q50 = median(Cc),
    q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time / week, q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 12, linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (weeks)", y = "Adalimumab Cc (mg/L)",
    title = "Simulated adalimumab concentrations (median and 5th-95th percentile)",
    caption = "Model prediction without residual error. Dashed line: 12 mg/L, the upper reporting limit of the source assay."
  )
```

# Steady-state troughs against the observed cohort

The paper reports no concentration-time profile or NCA, only the summary of
the observed troughs. The simulated maintenance troughs (the concentration
just before each dose from week 24 onward, model prediction without
residual error) are summarised below beside the observed values. The
observed mean excludes the 70 samples reported only as above 12 mg/L and so
understates the true mean; it also pools patients on both intervals and on
optimised doses, so it is context, not a target.

```{r troughs}
trough_tbl <- dose_tbl |>
  filter(time >= 24 * week) |>
  select(treatment, time)

troughs <- sim |>
  inner_join(trough_tbl, by = c("treatment", "time"))

trough_summary <- troughs |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Cc),
    sd = sd(Cc),
    median = median(Cc),
    pct_above_12 = 100 * mean(Cc > 12),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

trough_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = treatment,
    "Mean trough (mg/L)" = mean,
    "SD (mg/L)" = sd,
    "Median trough (mg/L)" = median,
    "% above 12 mg/L" = pct_above_12
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

Observed (Results 3.2): mean 9.57 mg/L (SD 5.70) over the maintenance
measurements, with 7.4% of all samples above 12 mg/L and unquantified. The
observed pooled mean lies between the two simulated arms, as expected for a
cohort in which most patients were on every-other-week dosing and the rest
had been intensified. The weekly arm's trough is higher despite its 21.8%
higher CL/F, because its dosing rate is twice as high.

```{r trough-check}
eow <- trough_summary$median[trough_summary$treatment == "40 mg every other week"]
# Structural: a mis-transcribed CL/F, V/F or dose unit moves the median by tens
# of percent; the band is wide because the observed summary is censored and
# pools regimens.
stopifnot(eow > 4, eow < 15)
```

# PKNCA steady-state exposure

```{r pknca}
tau_tbl <- tibble(
  treatment = c("40 mg every other week", "40 mg weekly"),
  start = c(end_time - 2 * week, end_time - week),
  end = end_time
)

conc_df <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)

intervals <- tau_tbl |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE) |>
  as.data.frame()

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)
```

At steady state the dosing-interval AUC equals the dose divided by CL/F, so
each patient's PKNCA Cav should equal 40 / (CL/F x tau) with that patient's
own CL/F. Patients with a long half-life (a large V/F draw) are not fully at
steady state by week 52 and the trapezoid rule adds a little error, so the
check is on the median and the 90th percentile rather than on every patient.

```{r pknca-check}
cl_ind <- sim |>
  filter(time == end_time) |>
  select(id, cl)

cav_chk <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  select(id, treatment, cav = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(tau_tbl, by = "treatment") |>
  left_join(cl_ind, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    cav_expected = 40 / (cl * (end - start)),
    pct_diff = 100 * (cav / cav_expected - 1)
  )

cav_chk |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(
    median_pct_diff = median(pct_diff),
    p90_abs_pct_diff = quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  abs(median(cav_chk$pct_diff)) < 5,
  quantile(abs(cav_chk$pct_diff), 0.9) < 15
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Inter-individual variability scale.** Table 4 reports IIV as a
  percentage (33.3% on CL/F, 53.8% on V/F) for exponential random effects.
  It is read on the standard-deviation scale, omega = CV/100, so the
  variances are 0.333^2 and 0.538^2. The alternative
  omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) gives 0.105 and 0.253, about 5% and 13% lower.
* **CRP at zero.** The log-linear term `1 + 0.075 * ln(CRP)` is undefined
  at CRP = 0 and the paper does not say how zero values were handled. Table
  2 reports a minimum of 0.00 mg/L, while the lowest ln(CRP) in Figure S1 is
  about -4.6, i.e. about 0.01 mg/L, which suggests zero values were floored
  near there. The model applies the published form as is; users must supply
  CRP > 0, and the virtual cohort here floors CRP at 0.01 mg/L.
* **CRP is not centred.** Equation (6) applies ln(CRP) without a reference
  value, so the typical CL/F of 0.334 L/day is for CRP = 1 mg/L. At the
  cohort mean CRP of 8.46 mg/L the typical CL/F is 16% higher.
* **Figure S1 axis unit.** Figure S1's y-axis is labelled 'CL (L/h)', but
  its values (about 0.3) match CL/F in L/day; L/day (Table 4) is used.
* **Dosing-interval covariate.** `REGI_QW` = 1 for weekly administration,
  matching the screened covariate 'dosing interval (one week or otherwise)'
  (Methods 2.4) and the Results statement that CL/F was 21.8% higher on
  weekly than on every-other-week dosing. The authors regard the effect as a
  marker of treatment intensification driven by disease activity rather
  than a causal effect of the interval (Discussion), so the model should not
  be used to predict the clearance change when one patient is switched to
  weekly dosing.
* **Time-varying covariates.** ADA status and CRP were recorded per
  monitoring occasion in the source and may be supplied as time-varying
  columns. The virtual cohort here holds them constant within a patient.
* **Censoring.** The source fit handled 15 below-limit samples with the M5
  method and 70 samples reported as above 12 mg/L as right-censored (M3).
  Those are estimation devices and are not part of the simulation model.
* **Base model.** Table 4 also lists a base model (no CRP or regimen
  effect; CL/F 0.376 L/day). Only the final model is packaged.
* **Evaluated literature models.** The eight models of Table 1 were
  re-implemented by the authors for external evaluation only and are not
  packaged from this paper; their primary publications are the right
  sources for them.
* No erratum was found for this article (PubMed and Europe PMC,
  checked 2026-11-15).
